image_description: A close-up view of a grey whale's head and upper torso emerging from the ocean surface. The whale is angled upwards, displaying its rostrum and blowholes. The skin is dark grey with characteristic white mottling (barnacles/lice). Water splashes around the lower jaw. No dorsal fin is visible, consistent with the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the arched rostrum typical of grey whales. While the blowholes are partially obscured by the angle and spray, the general head shape and positioning are correct for the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture exhibits the classic mottled pattern with distinct white callosities/barnacle patches, particularly on the top of the head and snout.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is cropped at the shoulders/neck region. The posterior back where dorsal knuckles would be located is outside the frame. However, the absence of a dorsal fin in the visible area is consistent.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior portion of the body is visible. The full spindle shape cannot be verified due to cropping and water occlusion.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the Head_and_Face checkpoint, the visible body skin shows accurate mottling and texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed or submerged; baleen plates are internal and not visible in this external shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are located further down the body and are completely submerged or out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is entirely out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The high-resolution texture on the snout and head clearly depicts the rough, bumpy texture associated with callosities and barnacles.

The horizon line is slightly uneven and blends softly into the sky, which is common in AI generations but not necessarily a structural failure. Very minor.
